data.title: EU chief pitches 'associate member' status for Canada
data.description: STRASBOURG (FRANCE) - EU chief Ursula von der Leyen raised the prospect Wednesday of Canada becoming the 27-nation bloc's first "associate member", as she pitched closer cooperation on tech, defence and energy to Canadian leader Mark Carney.

data.title: Turkish courts jail LGBTQ activists as crackdown widens
data.description: ISTANBUL - Turkish courts have jailed more LGBTQ activists and supporters, raising to 62 the number remanded in custody following a weekend crackdown, a legal rights group said on Wednesday.

data.title: Former Kosovo president convicted of war crimes
data.description: PRISTINA - Former Kosovo president Hashim Thaci, sentenced to 25 years in prison on Wednesday for war crimes, has long been seen within the Balkan country as a guerilla hero and symbol of its bloody independence struggle.

data.title: German state premier aims to halt far-right surge
data.description: ROSTOCK, Germany - Germany’s anti-immigration AfD party is eyeing another election triumph on Sunday in a northeastern coastal state where the popular premier is campaigning on a promise to hold back a rising far-right tide.

data.title: Turkish courts jails LGBTQ activists as crackdown widens
data.description: ISTANBUL - Turkish courts have jailed more LGBTQ activists and supporters, raising to 62 the number remanded in custody following a weekend crackdown, a legal rights group said on Wednesday.

data.title: EU considers ‘associate member’ status for Canada
data.description: STRASBOURG, France - EU chief Ursula von der Leyen raised the prospect Wednesday of Canada becoming the 27-nation bloc’s first “associate member’, as she pitched closer cooperation on technology, defence and energy to Canadian leader Mark Carney.

data.title: Amnesty documents ‘crimes against humanity’ by Iran in 2022
data.description: PARIS - Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in the crackdown on 2022 protests that left hundreds dead, Amnesty International said Wednesday, adding Tehran’s suppression of new demonstrations this year bore the “same hallmarks” but on an even wider scale.

data.title: Philippines’ ex-leader Duterte makes first appearance at ICC
data.description: MANILA — Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court (ICC) for the first time Wednesday, as he faces charges over his "war on drugs" that killed thousands.

data.title: China opens major canal linking landlocked regions to sea
data.description: BEIJING - China opened a major canal on Wednesday that will provide landlocked areas with direct access to the sea, state media said, reducing transport times and costs as the country aims to bolster trade ties with regional neighbours.

data.title: English village votes to 'secede' from UK over asylum centre
data.description: LONDON — An English village of around 350 people announced Wednesday that a vast majority of residents had voted yes in an "independence referendum" to protest plans to house over 1,200 migrants in a nearby facility.

data.title: Convicted crime lord plotted prison escape by clinging to a drone
data.description: HONG KONG — A South Korean crime lord convicted of murder in the Philippines reportedly planned to escape prison by strapping himself to a drone – until his own accomplice’s rehearsal footage gave the game away.

data.title: Brazilian voters the latest to eye Bukele security model with envy
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - Fed up with witnessing muggings in Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana neighbourhood, William Correia formed a volunteer group to patrol the streets and report robberies on social media.

data.title: Peace is a 'dangerous' word in Russian city heading to polls
data.description: TAMBOV (RUSSIA) - "Terrified" by escalating Ukrainian drone attacks, locals in the Russian city of Tambov head to parliamentary elections this weekend under no illusions that the pro-peace candidate stands a chance of victory.

data.title: EU chief to unveil social media, gaming curbs for under-15s
data.description: STRASBOURG (FRANCE) - EU chief Ursula von der Leyen will on Wednesday unveil long-awaited plans to protect children from online harm by curbing access to social media, video-sharing platforms, games and AI chatbots for under-15s.

data.title: Meta chief pushes back on AI slowdown calls
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg pushed back Tuesday against growing calls to pause or slow AI development, arguing that market incentives and legal liability are the best safeguards against the technology's risks.

data.title: Dead animals, barren fields, and hunger - El Nino chokes Central America
data.description: SAN LORENZO (HONDURAS) - Animals have been dropping dead amid the worst drought in living memory for many Central Americans, who are grappling with the unforgiving effects of the powerful El Nino weather pattern over the region.

data.title: Saudi says Houthis target Mecca, warn of 'red line'
data.description: RIYADH (SAUDI ARABIA) - The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis accused the rebels on Wednesday of targeting Islam's holy city Mecca, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region.

data.title: US touts its power, avoids Iran war at G20 Energy meeting
data.description: HOUSTON - The United States hammered home a message touting its energy dominance at Tuesday's meeting of G20 energy ministers in Houston, while brushing past the consequences of Washington's war in Iran and environmental concerns.

data.title: US military buildup in Palau stirs war fears
data.description: KOROR (PALAU) - US military plans to rebuild the main port in a pristine Pacific archipelago have stirred painful memories of World War II and have locals concerned about being caught in a potential superpower conflict.

data.title: Court orders N. Korea pay Seoul $32.5 mn for blowing up office
data.description: SEOUL - A Seoul court ordered Pyongyang on Wednesday to pay roughly US$32.5 million (1 billion baht) for blowing up in 2020 an office in North Korea that was intended to foster better relations between the two Koreas.

data.title: AI giants pursue self-regulation as safety fears mount
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The world's biggest AI companies are working on creating a standards body, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said on Tuesday, as fears rise about the dangers of AI and pressure is on to create a safer version of the technology.

data.title: South Africa intensifies hunt after eight women found dead
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - South African police are racing to crack the killings of at least eight women whose bodies have been found east of Johannesburg in two months, the latest on Tuesday.

data.title: Maduro ally pleads guilty to US money laundering charges
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Alex Saab, a former Venezuelan minister and close ally of ousted president Nicolas Maduro, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to money laundering under a deal with US prosecutors, court filings showed.

data.title: Finnish president Stubb speaks to AFP about Trump, Russia and saunas
data.description: HELSINKI - Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Donald Trump "pretty much does what he wants" and recommended staying calm in a world on edge, preferably with a sauna, in a freewheeling interview to AFP on Tuesday.

data.title: Empty benches as schools reopen in Venezuela's quake-hit Guaira
data.description: LA GUAIRA (VENEZUELA) - Schools in Venezuela's quake-scarred coastal state of La Guaira were deserted on Tuesday, a day after the start of the new school year, with many parents opting to keep children home for fear of further deadly tremors.

data.title: Trump says Kennedy Center to close after judge bars name change
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the Kennedy Center will close down -- possibly for good -- after a judge ruled his name cannot be added onto the famed arts institution's exterior.

data.title: Trump decries ‘horrible’ Supreme Court mail-in ballot ruling
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump assailed the Supreme Court on Tuesday after it denied his request to lift an order halting his divisive plan to restrict mail-in voting — accusing the court of allowing itself to be cowed by Democrats.

data.title: Brazil’s top court probes judge’s ties to jailed banker
data.description: BRASILIA - Brazil’s Supreme Court on Tuesday began examining one of its top justice’s ties to a jailed banker, in an unprecedented crisis that has eclipsed the country’s presidential election campaign.

data.title: Denmark says Russian frigate fired flares at helicopter
data.description: COPENHAGEN - Denmark and Russia were at a war of words Tuesday after Danish authorities accused a Russian frigate of firing flares at a Danish military helicopter.

data.title: China warns against space ‘battlefield’
data.description: PARIS - China on Tuesday warned against turning outer space into a “battlefield” and Russia said it must be “free from any weapon” after the United States confirmed for the first time that it has arms deployed in orbit above the Earth.

data.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
data.description: VILNIUS, Lithuania - NATO fighter jets shot down a drone over Lithuania, the Baltic state’s president said Tuesday, in the latest security incident on the alliance’s eastern flank during Russia’s war with Ukraine.

data.title: Ukraine winemakers defy war to make a splash at home
data.description: BEREHOVE — As this year's harvest season entered full swing, a winery in western Ukraine had an additional task to oversee: installing solar panels to help it weather blackouts caused by Russian military strikes.

data.title: Greek neo-Nazi exits prison, vows return to politics
data.description: DOMOKOS — The former spokesman of Greek neo-Nazi party Golden Dawn, Ilias Kasidiaris, was released from prison Tuesday and vowed a return to politics, having already drawn attention from Elon Musk.

data.title: Saudi Arabia vows to respond 'firmly' to Houthi attacks
data.description: SANAA — Saudi Arabia vowed Tuesday to respond "firmly" to attacks by Yemen's Houthis, after the Iran-backed fighters wounded 13 people in the kingdom in an assault using ballistic missiles and drones.

data.title: Beijing imposes total ban on drones after deadly crash
data.description: Beijing has introduced stricter drone regulations, banning all uncrewed flights as well as the possession and storage of existing devices, while detailing disposal methods for the first time in an effort to strengthen security in the capital.

data.title: US military confirms Iran war has led to munitions shortfall
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The United States is facing a shortfall in ammunition as a result of its war against Iran, the Defense Department's inspector general confirmed Monday, contrasting with President Donald Trump's assertions of full stocks.

data.title: Berlin's run-down public spaces at heart of election campaign
data.description: BERLIN — Politicians campaigning for Sunday's Berlin state election have painted an unflattering picture of the German capital, vowing to clear garbage-strewn streets and promising "syringe-free playgrounds".
